source.title: Few-shot regulatory sequence design with a genomic language model
source.authors: Yu-Kun A. Hao; Matthew Liu; Divya Nori; G. Brixi; Thomas K. Lau; C. Ramakrishnan; Daniel T. Chang; Ryan Park; William E. Allen; Brian L. Hie

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including Methods and supplementary figure captions, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether candidate induction heads contribute to in-context sequence generation using attention-head identification and ablation in Evo 2; the outcome is predicted enhancer activity, not the original natural-language loss measure.
record.gate_note: The study identifies candidate induction heads and reports ablation outcomes for generated enhancer activity. It does not test training-time onset, a loss-curve bump, token-index loss, or the specific [A][B] → [B] copying operation and prior-token-head composition. Categorical-Jacobian and sparse-autoencoder analyses concern example influence or prompt-structure features, not the specified induction-head mechanism. No cited results from other studies are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper identifies candidate induction heads in Evo 2 1B and 7B (DNA models) and ablates them. This gives a result bearing on whether induction-like heads appear in a non-text model (V4) and on whether they carry in-context generation. It does not test formation, composition, or the [A][B]…[A]→[B] circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is roughly right. The authors say some attention heads are causally linked to inductive generation and ICL in Evo 2, which suggests genomic ICL may originate from induction. They caution that this does not fully resolve the mechanism and that distributed or redundant circuits may contribute.
record.recipe_differences: Uses repeated-pattern and separator-based attention-head screening and head ablation, but applies them to genomic sequence generation and predicted enhancer activity rather than testing natural-language induction behavior with the original loss-based measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size (Evo 2 1B versus 7B) and number of in-context enhancer examples (2, 4, 8, 16, 32) are varied. The text provides significance values for 1B at 4 and 8 shots, and for 7B at 2, 4, and 8 shots.
record.problems: Head identification and ablation outcomes are presented as plots without numerical activity values in the text. Ablation evidence uses predicted enhancer activity rather than a direct measurement of [A][B] → [B] copying; no previous-token-head composition or training-time phase-change test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing the listed versions were left out. Categorical-Jacobian and sparse-autoencoder analyses were not entered as rows because they measure example influence or prompt-structure features rather than induction-head behavior or the listed version-specific outcomes.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head, [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying, and small attention-only setting; Evo 2 is a large hybrid model.
Other model families, training runs, architectures and modalities beyond Evo 2 1B/7B; whether the heads actually show token-level induction behaviour.

missing.what: Numeric induction-head scores and predicted-activity values for intact, induction-ablated and control conditions
Statistics for 1B at 2, 16 and 32 shots and 7B at 16 and 32 shots, and the intact-model baseline for 7B

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 'supports' label should be dropped, because the study never tests composition or copying, or the small attention-only setting. Control rows (r8-r12, r18-r22) should not carry version links. The text calls the heads 'candidate' induction heads, and the 1B ablation covers a single head.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish composition with an earlier previous-token head or directly test [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying. Evo 2 is not described as a small attention-only transformer.
Tests Evo 2 1B and 7B only; other model families, training runs, architectures, and modalities are not tested.

relationships.condition: Evo 2 1B (4- and 8-shot, p=0.023 and 0.040) and Evo 2 7B (2-, 4- and 8-shot), DNA enhancer generation
relationships.reason: Heads picked by a repeated-sequence/separator attention screen exist in both sizes, and ablating them lowers predicted enhancer activity versus same-layer controls (r1-r2, r4-r5, r13-r15). This is weaker than a full induction demonstration: it uses a modified score and a proxy outcome, and the 1B result is a single head.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating attention-screened heads lowers predicted enhancer activity relative to same-layer controls in both sizes, using a modified induction score and a single head at 1B.

relation.reason: Repeated-DNA and separator attention screening identifies candidate heads in two Evo 2 sizes; their ablation reduces predicted enhancer activity relative to controls.

tranche.reason: The study screens and causally ablates candidate induction heads in genomic models, providing a result on V4 in a DNA generation setting.
